status: registered before validation results were seen; development split used only to fit the regression
hypothesis: Per-sex linear regressions on stature and mass (body-anatomy predictSegmentLengths) predict derived segment lengths of unseen ANSUR II subjects with a mean absolute percentage error of at most 5% and a 90th-percentile absolute percentage error of at most 12% for every primary segment, and are no worse than fixed stature ratios for every segment where a published ratio exists.
falsification: Any primary segment exceeding either threshold on the validation split, or any ratio-covered segment where the regression MAPE exceeds the fixed-ratio MAPE, fails the protocol. Thresholds are not changed after seeing validation results; a new protocol version is registered instead.

data.name: ANSUR II public working databases (2012)
data.publisher: U.S. Army Natick Soldier RD&E Center; cleared for unlimited public release
data.obtainedFrom: GitHub mirror senihberkay/US-Army-ANSUR-II, files 'ANSUR II MALE Public.csv' and 'ANSUR II FEMALE Public.csv' (fetched 2026-11-06; the original site was unreachable from the build environment)
data.units: lengths in mm; weightkg column is hectograms; converted to m and kg
data.limitation: Military personnel aged roughly 17-58; not representative of a civilian population. Sexes analysed separately. Raw files are not committed.

split.rule: subjectid even = development (regression fit), subjectid odd = validation (one-shot confirmation)
split.note: After the validation split has been seen once it is a regression check, not fresh confirmation.

model: segmentLengthM = b0 + b1 * statureM + b2 * massKg (ordinary least squares, development split)

mape.definition: mean over validation subjects of |predicted - measured| / measured

p90ape.definition: 90th percentile over validation subjects of |predicted - measured| / measured

vsFixedRatio.definition: regression MAPE <= fixed-ratio MAPE on the same subjects
vsFixedRatio.appliesTo: every primary segment with a fixed ratio below

fixedRatioBaseline.source: Drillis & Contini (1966) segment length ratios of stature as commonly tabulated (e.g. Winter, Biomechanics and Motor Control of Human Movement). Basis R for the ratios; the correspondence to ANSUR landmarks is approximate (shoulder width in that table is wider than biacromial breadth; trunk is acromion-to-trochanter).

claims: Passing upgrades the morphology axis at level 1 to M for the derived segment lengths relative to this military sample only. It says nothing about surface shape, circumference placement, civilian populations, children, or other axes.
